title: Fischer-Tropsch synthesis (FTS) reference family
reaction: n CO + (2n+1) H2 -> CnH(2n+2) + n H2O (alkanes) | n CO + 2n H2 -> CnH2n + n H2O (alkenes)
objective: Optional literature-backed family for syngas-to-hydrocarbons Fischer-Tropsch screening. Candidates compare a Co/Al2O3 high-temperature anchor (the canonical commercial benchmark), an Fe/SiO2 lower-olefin route, and a Co/CNT structured-support emerging variant.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Balance catalyst cost, evidence quality, route maturity, and reported selectivity / chain-length performance.

cost-first.label: Cost-first
cost-first.description: Bias ranking toward catalyst cost while preserving route and evidence guardrails.

evidence-first.label: Evidence-first
evidence-first.description: Reward stronger literature support and more reproducible Co / Fe FT preparation routes.

citations.label: J. Catal. 2007
citations.note: Chu, Chernavskii et al.: cobalt species in promoted Co / alumina-supported FT catalysts, characterising the active Co0 phase and reduction window.

citations.label: Catal. Today 2009
citations.note: Khodakov: foundational review of cobalt FT catalysts linking nanoparticle structure to catalytic performance, the canonical Co-FT structure-activity reference.

citations.label: Appl. Catal. A 2010
citations.note: Trepanier, Dalai et al.: CNT-supported cobalt nanoparticle FT catalysts, demonstrating how carbon-nanotube supports change reducibility and selectivity vs alumina.

citations.label: Top. Catal. 2013
citations.note: Melaet, Lindeman et al.: cobalt particle-size effects in FT and in CO2 hydrogenation, mapping the activity / selectivity dependence on Co nanoparticle dimensions.

citations.label: Catal. Today 2014
citations.note: Todic, Ma et al.: CO-insertion mechanism kinetic model for FT over Re-promoted Co, providing a transferable kinetic baseline for Co-based reactor screening.

citations.label: ChemCatChem 2016
citations.note: Oschatz, Lamme et al.: ordered mesoporous materials as supports for stable iron catalysts in Fischer-Tropsch synthesis of lower olefins.

citations.label: Chem 2018
citations.note: Wang, Xia et al.: Fischer-Tropsch synthesis steps into the solar era, demonstrating syngas-to-lower-olefin conversion under photothermal conditions.

route_templates.name: Co / Al2O3 FT cobalt route
route_templates.route_note: Most transferable FT basis matching the dominant commercial Co / Al2O3 catalysts (Sasol / Shell-style).

route_templates.name: Fe / SiO2 lower-olefin FT route
route_templates.manufacturing_mode: Iron-based FT catalyst targeting lower olefins
route_templates.route_note: Iron-based FT route biased toward C2-C4 olefins, complementary to the Co route which favors heavier paraffins.

route_templates.name: Co / CNT structured-support FT route
route_templates.manufacturing_mode: Cobalt on carbon-nanotube support FT route
route_templates.route_note: Cobalt on CNT support; structured carbon increases Co dispersion at the cost of CNT support overhead.

candidates.title: Co / Al2O3 FT (commercial baseline)
candidates.summary: Cobalt supported on alumina with Re or Pt promoter; the dominant low-temperature FT commercial catalyst basis (Sasol / Shell GTL).
decision_notes: Most transferable FT basis and the clearest commercial comparison point for low-temperature GTL.
Catalyst economics dominated by Co loading and Re / Pt promoter; alumina support is a small fraction of cost.

pricing.note: Live Co feed with a precursor / conversion markup for commercial Co / Al2O3 FT screening.
Live Re feed with a precursor / conversion markup.
Gamma-alumina cost on engineering proxy comparable to commercial Sasol / BASF ranges.

candidates.title: Fe / SiO2 lower-olefin FT
candidates.summary: Iron on mesoporous silica targeting C2-C4 olefins via high-temperature FT, an alternative to Co-FT when olefins are the desired product.
decision_notes: Best fit when the program target is lower olefins (C2=-C4=) rather than heavier paraffins.
Iron is far cheaper than cobalt but methane selectivity is higher; promoter (K, Mn) discipline matters.

pricing.note: Live Fe feed with a precursor / conversion markup for Fe-FT screening.
Potassium promoter cost held on a derived screening proxy.
Mesoporous silica cost held on engineering proxy comparable to commercial silica gel ranges.

candidates.title: Co / CNT structured FT
candidates.summary: Cobalt on carbon-nanotube support exploiting CNT architecture for tunable Co dispersion and reducibility.
decision_notes: Use this when CNT-support architecture is acceptable and tighter Co dispersion control is desired.
Catalyst economics shift toward CNT support cost; active-Co reducibility window is wider than alumina-supported.

pricing.note: Live Co feed with a precursor / conversion markup.
Multi-walled CNT support cost held on engineering proxy reflecting structured-carbon premium.
